the magnetoresonant properties of granular magnetic nanocomposite materials with carbon matrices are determined by iron/cobalt nanoparticles formed in the course of their synthesis.
the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) in granular nanocomposites with carbon matrices is determined by the presence of iron carbide and cobalt carbide nanoparticles.
the magnetoresonant properties of nanogranule systems are determined by the presence of iron/cobald carbide nanoparticles.

the magnetoresonant spectra of the studied nanocomposite systems are characterized by a wide resonance peak with a half-width of 0.6–1.2 kOe, a low resonance field of 0.3–1.5 kOe, and a small value of the effective magnetization of 0.2–0.3 kG.

the magnetoresonant properties of nanocomposite systems are determined by the formation of iron and cobalt carbides in the carbon matrix.
